sources.name: ICRISAT broad bed and furrow system

practices.summary: Follow a cereal or oilseed with a nitrogen-fixing pulse to rebuild soil nitrogen and break pest cycles.
Grow rows of pigeon pea, green gram or cowpea between main-crop rows for nitrogen, cover and income insurance.

names.en: Keep crop residue as mulch (no burning)

practices.summary: Leave chopped residue on the surface to cut evaporation, feed soil life and avoid the soil and air damage of burning.
Sow directly into the previous crop's stubble with a zero-till drill to save moisture, fuel and soil structure.
Sow rainfed crops only when the seed zone is moist enough, to avoid failed germination and re-sowing costs.
Walk the field weekly, use pheromone and sticky traps, and act on thresholds rather than calendar spraying.
Raised beds with furrows on heavy black soils drain excess water in wet spells and hold moisture in dry spells.
Clear furrows and field outlets before heavy rain so roots are not waterlogged.
Deliver water to the root zone to cut groundwater pumping for water-hungry crops.
Grow a fast legume for 45-50 days and incorporate it before the main crop to add organic matter and nitrogen.
Drill rice seed instead of puddled transplanting to save irrigation water and labour.
Let paddy water drop below the soil surface before re-irrigating, saving water and cutting methane.
Coat pulse seed with the matching Rhizobium culture to boost biological nitrogen fixation.
Add well-decomposed compost or farmyard manure to raise organic carbon and water-holding capacity.
Spread detrashed cane leaves between rows instead of burning to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
Plant on raised beds for drainage and efficient furrow or drip irrigation.
